Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Apex Medical Devices Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO; Lisa Chen, CFO; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Medical Devices achieved record results this quarter, reflecting the strength of our diversified portfolio and our commitment to innovation.

Today, I will cover eight key aspects of our performance: the key assumptions underlying our guidance, trends in our capital equipment versus consumables mix, progress on R&D investment and our innovation pipeline, organic revenue growth by segment and geography, SG&A expense management and the efficiency gains we've realized, our strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter, our revenue and margin guidance for the coming periods, and adoption rates in hospitals and ambulatory surgery centers.

Lisa will then provide a more detailed review of our financials, Raj will update us on our technology advancements, and Tom will discuss our market strategies. We'll then conclude with a Q&A session.

Now, let's get started with the key assumptions underlying our guidance. Our full-year 2024 outlook, which we introduced last quarter and are reaffirming today, calls for revenue between $4.85 billion and $4.95 billion, or 9% to 11% organic growth at the midpoint. We're also targeting adjusted gross margin expansion of 150 basis points to 68.5%, along with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $5.85 to $6.05. These figures are based on a disciplined approach informed by strong visibility into procedural trends, reimbursement environments, and our solid innovation pipeline.

To unpack this, consider the main drivers: procedural volumes and market dynamics, pricing and mix effects, performance across regions, our cost structure and supply chain stability, and key strategic elements. Our major franchises—Cardiovascular at 45% of revenue, Orthopedics at 30%, and Endoscopy & Robotics at 25%—mirror dynamics seen in leaders like Medtronic's TAVR leadership, Stryker's Mako robotics, and Boston Scientific's Watchman LAAO devices.

Procedural volumes and demand are the top revenue driver, with mid-single-digit growth assumed across core areas, continuing the post-COVID recovery in elective procedures. In U.S. cardiology, we project 6-8% growth in TAVR and structural heart procedures, powered by expanded indications for our ApexFlow transcatheter valve, which earned FDA approval via the PMA pathway using SSED based on the Sapien 3 dataset. We're forecasting 12,000 to 13,000 annual U.S. TAVR implants for our lineup, up from 11,000 in 2023, backed by ACC/AHA guidelines promoting earlier intervention for low-risk patients. LAAO closures similar to Watchman FLX are set for 8% growth, aided by Medicare's NTAP reimbursement extension.

In orthopedics, U.S. hip and knee procedures should rise 5-7%, driven by aging Baby Boomers reaching peak implant age and our Triad cementless stem launching in Q1 2024 after 510(k) clearance. Global hip/knee volumes are expected at 1.8 million procedures according to IFU data, with our Mako-integrated robotics aiming for 15% U.S. market share, up from 13%. For endoscopy and robotics, growth of 10-12% factors in accelerated adoption like da Vinci systems via our EndoBot single-port platform, which has CE Mark and is enrolling 500 patients in its U.S. IDE trial. Market research from Grand View projects a 20% CAGR for robotic-assisted GI procedures through 2028.

These projections draw from IQVIA and Definitive Healthcare data through Q3 2023, showing U.S. volumes 2-3% ahead of earlier models, tempered by minor seasonal flu effects on scheduling.

On pricing and product mix, we anticipate flat to +1% impact on average selling prices. U.S. core ASPs should rise 0.5%, with GPO consolidation like Vizient and Premier renewals at flat pricing offset by premium shifts. Our advanced cardiology offerings, including bioresorbable scaffolds similar to Abbott's Absorb follow-on, carry 5-7% premiums. Orthopedic robotic kits add 8-10% to system ASPs. In Europe, 1-2% erosion from HTA pressures like NICE TAVR reviews is balanced by 3% VBP uplift in China for endoscopy.

Regionally, organic growth assumptions are U.S. at 10-12%, EMEA 6-8%, APAC 8-10%, and Rest of World 12-15%. The U.S., 65% of revenue, assumes stable CMS FY2024 IPPS TAVR MS-DRG weights at 1.2x prior year and no cuts to pass-through for premium valves, with electives normalizing to 98% of pre-COVID by Q2 2024. EMEA at 20% sees easing MDR hurdles after 2023 recertifications, with 7% growth including 9% TAVR volume increases in Germany/UK from INTRIDE trial results. APAC at 12% projects 15% growth from 75% China localization for orthopedics via NMPA Class III approvals, despite 5% forex drag at CNY/USD 7.2; India/Japan endoscopy up 12% on expansions. Rest of World at 3% gets $50 million upside from LatAm/Brazil TAVR tenders. Overall FX is a 2% headwind at EUR/USD 1.08, JPY/USD 145.

Cost-wise, gross margin expands from COGS discipline: raw materials like titanium and platinum-iridium up 3-4%, offset by dual-sourcing in Mexico and Ireland after semiconductor issues, pushing factory utilization to 85% from 80% for 200 bps leverage. OpEx sees R&D at 12.5% or $610 million funding five Phase III trials like AFib neuromodulation akin to Medtronic's Symplicity; SG&A flat at 28% via digital sales tools cutting rep travel 15%. Supply chain assumes no disruptions, inventory at 120 days from 140, with Q4 Taiwan chips on schedule.

Strategically, we bake in 100-150 bps market share gains from launches like 20% U.S. penetration for ApexFlow by year-end 2024 and $200-300 million tuck-in M&A. Tailwinds include GLP-1 drugs boosting orthopedics mobility demand. Risks: 2% revenue sensitivity to U.S. procedure weakness, reimbursement audits under 5%, 50 bps EPS from 1% inflation overrun. Upside from early EndoBot commercialization or structural heart deals.

These conservative assumptions, drawn from proprietary forecasts, IDN insights, and surgeon surveys, position us strongly in a $600 billion-plus devices market growing 5-6% with minimally invasive and value-based care shifts.

Now, let's talk about capital equipment versus consumables mix trends. In our business, capital equipment includes high-value upfront systems like the PrecisionNav robotic navigation platform and EchoVue ultrasound suites, while consumables deliver recurring annuities from single-use endoscopic tools, biopsy kits, and ablation catheters. This razor-razorblade model fuels predictable, high-margin revenue as our installed base expands and utilization rises.

In Q3, the mix was 38% capital and 62% consumables, improved from 42/58% prior year. Year-to-date, consumables hit 60% of revenue, up 450 basis points, with 14% organic consumables growth versus 8% capital. Consumables ASP held at $1,250 per kit amid 16% global procedure surge from expanded PrecisionNav indications in ortho and neuro.

Post-pandemic, capital rebounded in H1 with IDN orders like Kaiser and HCA for EchoVue 4K, but moderated to mid-single digits as backlogs cleared. Consumables grew 19% to $285 million from a 22% YoY installed base increase to 4,200 PrecisionNav systems, averaging 28 procedures per unit monthly, up from 24.

U.S. consumables at 65% mix benefit from 4-6% CMS OPPS boosts for robotics. Europe at 55% faced DRG and MDR costs but gained 12% from FlexiCath ablation CE Mark in EP cases. APAC, up 25% YoY, skewed 52% consumables from China EchoVue tenders and Japan's neuroendoscopy kits for 1.2 million annual procedures by 2027.

We're optimizing with PrecisionNav Gen3 AI navigation cutting times 15%, lifting attachment to 95%; U.S. pilot shows 20% instrument use. Bioresorbable consumables for CV interventions target H2 2025 FDA, echoing Intuitive's da Vinci 80%+ consumables and Boston's Watchman pull-through.

This mix expands gross margins to 68.5% from 66.2%, guiding consumables to 63-65% in FY24 on mid-teens procedures. Commercial efforts include KOLs, UnitedHealthcare value contracts, and expansions in Galway and Singapore.

This annuity shift de-risks us amid macro pressures, setting up 10-12% organic growth in 2025.

Moving on to R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress. Our R&D remains central to growth in a competitive landscape against Boston Scientific, Abbott, Stryker, under FDA PMA, EU MDR, and NMPA scrutiny.

Q3 R&D was $285 million or 11.2% of $2.54 billion revenue, up 14% YoY and 8% sequentially. Full-year guide $1.15 billion or 10.8% of $10.6 billion, above initial due to 150 engineer hires in neuromodulation/robotics. Above 8-9% industry average per PwC; like Intuitive's 12-13%.

Allocation: 42% structural heart/EP (up from 38%), 28% robotics/AI, 20% ortho/spine, rest diagnostics/drug-devices. Efficiency: $45 million per IDE/PMA, down 7% via digital twins/AI testing.

Q3 hit 92% milestones: five submissions, three FDA IDEs across 28 programs.

Cardiovascular: InnoStent RB-2 in pivotal IDE with 400+ patients, 95% radial strength at 12 months vs. Absorb's 88%; Q4 2025 PMA. WATCHMAN FLX Pro-like LAAC EU MDR done June, live 15 markets, 28% stroke reduction.

EP: PULSE AI mapping like CARTO 3, IDE pivotal 98% success; year-end 510(k) for $4.2B market at 9% CAGR. China NMPA July, Singapore data 15% faster procedures.

Robotics: InnoBot Xi 85% integrated, Q1 2025 first-in-human CE fast-track; $120M YTD with NVIDIA haptics for $12B market 18% CAGR.

Orthopedics: Trinity Cementless 2,000 U.S. implants, 96% survivorship vs. Zimmer's 94%; Japan PMDA May unlocks $150M.

Diagnostics: GlucoSense Pro CGM 510(k) Type 2, 14-day wear MARD 8.2%; Q3 U.S. launch, India pilots 22% adherence.

Navigating FDA scrutiny up 20%, supply inflation; tailwinds CMS value-care, 15% R&D for M&A like $200M Euro valve tuck-in. U.S. 55%, Europe 25%, Asia 20% focus.

Pipeline supports 8-10% growth to 2027, six $500M+ blockbusters in AI/robotics/personalized tech.

Next, organic revenue growth by segment and geography. Excluding M&A, divestitures, FX, Q3 organic growth was 8.2% to $2.85 billion, full-year 7.6% to $10.9 billion—top of our 6-8% algorithm.

By segment, against Edwards, Stryker, Medtronic:

Cardiovascular (45%): Q3 12.5%, FY 10.8% on $1.28B. Structural heart 18% from 25%+ EvoValve Pro TAVR procedures, 22% U.S. share post S-3/low-risk indications. Coronary 9% on XcelStent 4% ASP. EP offset by PulseAI 15% adoption. $150M FY24 R&D bioresorbables for 12-15% structural growth, 15% TAVR CAGR.

Orthopedics/Spine (25%): Q3 6.8%, FY 5.9% $712M. Robotics 22% OrthoBotix in 450 U.S. hospitals, 18% robotic knees +300bps vs. Mako. Hip/knee 5% cementless porous reducing revisions 20%. Spine 4% biologics. Supply resilience +2% volume. Q1 FY24 AI planning for mid-teens robotics.

Minimally Invasive (20%): Q3 7.2%, FY 6.4% $570M. Endoscopy 11% FlexScope single-use +30% amid CRE. Hernia 5% bioabsorbable. SurgiBot 15% robotics, $200M APAC telesurgery.

Diabetes/Wearables (10%): Q3 4.5%, FY 4.1% $285M. GlucoFlow 2.0 8% 12% adherence app. Flat insulin, pivot closed-loop GLP-1 for 10% FY24.

Geography: U.S. 55% 9.1% Q3/8.4% FY, 12% elective >2019, 150bps share, 65% GPO Vizient/Premier.

EMEA 20% 6.7%/5.9%, Germany/UK 9% OrthoBotix NICE; France 3% improved Paris hub, MDR edge endoscopy +2pts.

APAC 18% 7.9%/6.8%, China 15% post-COVID TAVR 15% share; Japan 5% robotics, India 25% local mfg. 10%+ ASEAN telemed.

LATAM/Other 7% 4.2%/3.7%, Brazil recovery Mexico expansion value-shift.

Reflects high-single-digit volumes, 1-2% pricing/mix, 12 FY23 launches $450M incremental. $2.5B cash for M&A, 18% R&D. FY24 7-9% organic, AI/heart upside.

Then, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains. We've protected margins while funding innovation like robotics/neuromodulation akin to Evolution vs. Abbott Infinity.

Q3 SG&A $1.42B, +2.1% YoY reported, flat constant currency; 24.8% of revenue vs. 27.2%, 240bps delever. Third straight sequential gain, FY 25-26% vs. 28% FY23. YTD $185M savings >$150M target 23%.

Selling 62% $881M +1.8% YoY, 15% lower cost/rep-quarter. G&A $539M -3.4% procurement/digitization. Structural vs. Stryker's 26%.

Sales optimization: U.S. field headcount -8%, rev/rep +12% $2.8M ann. AI Salesforce Einstein/MedConnect prioritizes surgeons, non-selling time 45%->35% telematics. Like Intuitive da Vinci.

U.S. 26.1% vs. 29.4% structural heart +7% procedures FDA TAVR. EMEA 23.5% -310bps UK/Nordics merge $12M, Italy digital. APAC 21.2% vs. 25.8% China e-com WeChat -28% travel.

G&A procurement $92M Ariba indirects: IT Dell -17%, logistics Maersk -14% ISO. 15 data centers to 3 AWS, -31% cyber for 5G MiniMed vs. Tandem t:slim.

ZBB 85% lines, -$45M legacy ESC/TCT to virtual MedTech Hub. SAP ML 92% accruals like Boston Watchman.

Automation UiPath 65% invoices $18B chain -$28M 1.2M hours. Workday AI HR -19% recruiters 2,500 hires Vercise DBS.

Reinvest 60% $110M VAC endoscopy $15B vs. Olympus/Ethicon, Assert IQ vs. Reveal LINQ. Op margin +190bps 28.4%, 1000bps/5yrs >Evaluate avg.

FY25-26 $200-250M more Enterprise Roadmap. Risks fees/FX LATAM ANVISA; 6-8% procedures aging/China VBP for 100-150bps delever.

Now, strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter. After Q3's 14% organic from 18% structural heart/endoscopy double-digits, Q4 priorities align with Innovate/Expand/Operate pillars. Q4 revenue $1.45-1.50B 9-12% YoY, EBITDA 28.5-29% +150bps.

1. Commercial in heart/robotics (60% Q4 rev): EvoFlow 3.0 TAVR 20% faster/15% lower leak vs. Sapien; U.S. 25% growth CMS outpatient/50 centers. APAC China Q4 early 30% vs. Q3 200 reps 25% aortic market. FlexArm robotics AI haptics -30% fatigue, U.S. installs +40% to 1,200 vs. Intuitive.

2. Pipeline/R&D $220M +10% seq: NeuroScan AI epilepsy 95% predict -25% SUDEP FDA Breakthrough Q4 PMA vs. Percept. MakoEdge ortho haptics -18% OR $28k ASP EU CE 20% Germany. MedConnect RPM cloud $50M SaaS 100 ACOs 15% +22% outpatient CMS domestic API -35% lead.

3. EM expansion/reimbursement (20% driver): India Apollo 500 VizPulse endoscopy 40% lower infection 28% CAGR hep. Brazil ANVISA stents $2B $1.2k ASP. U.S. 10% +15% vol -2-3% GPO. Europe 12% 90% MDR vs. 70%. APAC/EM 22% China JV. NTAP NeuroScan +30% like Mako.

4. OpEx/margins $50M cost-out: 90/10 domestic 5%->2% inflation. AI sales -25% ramp 22% rev. ESG 20% Scope3 reusable 2-3% premium EU Green.

Q4 sets 15%+ H2, heart/robotics 60% incr. Risks 5% Euro/staffing offset 18-mo procedure lead. $3.2B liquidity 8-10x digital M&A.

Next, revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year. Looking to Q4 FY2023 and full FY2024, guidance reflects procedure momentum, product ramps, discipline.

Q4 revenue $2.45-2.50B, organic 8-9%, total 9-10% vs. Q3 $2.38B 7% organic CV/ortho. FY2024 raised $9.85-10.00B organic 7.5-8.5%, total 8.5-9.5% from $9.70-9.90B on U.S. procedures/next-gen.

Segments: CV 42% Q4 mid-teens organic, structural 10-12% Aurora TAVR 28% U.S. share vs. Sapien +15% vol Medicare low-risk Mayo. EP 20%+ RhythmSync AFib vs. DiamondTemp.

MedSurg 28% low double-digit, endoscopy 12-14% VisioFlex single-use post-COVID. Robotics PrecisionArm 25% util 85% >Intuitive elective norm.

Ortho/Spine 25% high-single, hips/knees 9% Triad 98% 5yr registry. Spine 11% biologics Mako-like.

Neuro/Vision mid-single NeuroStim vs. Infinity.

Regions: U.S. 55% 9-10% 98% pre-COVID Vizient +2-3% premium ASP. EMEA 25% 6-7% Germany/France offset UK NHS TAVR. APAC 15% 12-14% China 18% JV NMPA Aurora 1.5M cases. EM India/Brazil 15% dist.

$250M BioPulse PFA EP +$50M FY24 30% margins. Six PMA incl. bioresorb stents vs. Evolut.

Margins: Q4 adj gross 66-67% +50bps seq/100-150 YoY FY 66.5-67.5% +125bps. Mix +200bps heart/robotics 75%+ vs. 60%; resin -8% Mexico dual Red Sea; inventory 410 days JIT; +1.5-2% ASP no J&J Ottava erosion.

Op margin Q4 24.5-25.0% + from 23.8% SG&A 24% -75bps digital 40% virtual. R&D 12-13% $1.15B 25 programs AI OrthoScan. FY op 25.0-25.5% $2.48-2.55B op inc. EPS $5.25-5.35 190M sh 15% tax.

Capex $450M 4.6% Galway/Pittsburgh robotics. FCF $1.8-1.9B $1.2B div/buyback. FX 1% hedge 80%.

Risks elective inflation CMS stable, titanium Stryker recycle, China regs. Diversified 70% recurring <10% single prod.

Raising guide top-tier vs. Medtronic/Boston 5-6% Evaluate innovation/ops.

Finally, hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates. For PrecisionNav AI navigation/robotics ortho/neuro-spine, adoption proxies installed growth, service recurring, disposables 62% segment rev.

Q3 blended 48% of 1,200 U.S. hospitals/800 ASCs +12pts YoY/4 seq >20 cases/qtr.

Hospitals 52% +11pts, IDNs HCA/Tenet 18 new contracts 150 ORs. v2.5 AI haptics -22% time PROSPECT CMS NTAP.

ASCs 38% +18pts site-neutral OPPS 42 new installs Surgical Care/Regent 35% higher util dispos $2.8k +15% bundle.

Trends: U.S. hospitals Tier1 68% Mayo/Cleveland complex mm accuracy; community 39% leasing closes 25%. ASCs anterior cervical +28% YoY >15% Definitive.

EMEA 32% Germany/UK 41% DRG CE Spine. APAC 25% Japan NHI kypho China Q4 NMPA 50 ASCs Shanghai/Beijing. LatAm 12% Brazil SUS +10-15% global.

PrecisionNav Connect Epic/Cerner predict +18% throughput 85% service. TCO $1.2M/5yrs -30% vs. da Vinci/Mako.

Semicon delay 8% dual TSMC/Samsung. Site-neutral advocacy AdvaMed.

Guide 55% YE +22% base $280M dispos incr $15B TAM 14% CAGR Grand View.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa for a review of our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael. As Michael outlined comprehensively, we delivered exceptional financial performance this quarter, with the aspects he covered underscoring our robust revenue drivers, margin discipline, and forward momentum. To recap key financials, Q3 revenue hit $2.85 billion, up 8.2% organically, driven by the procedural growth and mix shifts detailed. Gross margins reached 68.5%, expanded by high-margin consumables and efficiencies. Adjusted operating margins improved to 28.4%, aided by SG&A deleveraging. Non-GAAP EPS was strong, aligning with our trajectory toward the raised FY2024 guide of $9.85-10.00 billion revenue, 66.5-67.5% gross, and $5.25-5.35 EPS. Expenses remain controlled, with R&D at 11.2% supporting pipeline wins, and capex focused on capacity. For Q4, we see continued 8-9% organic growth, with full-year risks mitigated by our balance sheet. Overall, profitability is resilient, positioning us for sustained EPS expansion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. We are excited about the progress we are making in our technology roadmap. Our latest innovation, ApexFlow 2.0, is poised to transform structural heart interventions with enhanced deployment and leak reduction. We expect FDA approval in Q4.

Building on Michael's R&D overview, our 28 programs are advancing rapidly, with 92% milestone hits. Key highlights include InnoStent RB-2's IDE enrollment, PULSE AI's pivotal success targeting EP growth, InnoBot Xi's integration nearing first-in-human, Trinity's implant milestones, and GlucoSense's launch. These, plus initiatives like NeuroScan and MakoEdge, reinforce our leadership in AI, robotics, and personalized devices, supporting 8-10% revenue contribution long-term. Supply chain and regulatory navigations keep us on track for multiple approvals.

Next, Tom with insights on our commercial strategy.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Raj. We are focused on driving commercial excellence and expanding our global reach. Our strategic partnerships are enabling us to access new markets and customer segments, as Michael noted in adoption, growth, and priorities. U.S. IDN contracts and GPO coverage at 65% fuel procedure ramps, while APAC JVs and EM expansions like India/Brazil target 20%+ growth. Value-based deals with payers tie to outcomes, boosting robotics and endoscopy uptake. KOL engagements and digital tools enhance rep productivity, aligning with consumables pull-through and 10-12% organic targets. We're leveraging site-neutral shifts for ASCs and MDR moats in Europe.

Now, back to Michael for Q&A.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Tom. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star one. Our first question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee - JPMorgan:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Michael, on the key assumptions for FY2024 guidance, particularly procedural volumes in U.S. cardiology and any sensitivity to reimbursement changes—could you elaborate on the offsets if volumes come in softer?

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Great question, David. As I detailed, we're assuming 6-8% TAVR/structural growth based on IQVIA data ahead of models, with stable CMS MS-DRGs and NTAP. If U.S. procedures soften 2%, that's about 2% revenue sensitivity, but offset by pricing/mix +1%, share gains from ApexFlow 20% penetration, and APAC upside like China 15%. Our conservative stance and $200-300M M&A firepower provide buffers. Confident at midpoint.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter - Goldman Sachs:
Thanks. Lisa, the consumables mix shift to 62%—impressive. Can you discuss utilization trends and if robotics capacity constraints could cap Q4 growth?

Lisa Chen:
Emily, thanks. Utilization at 28 procedures/unit/month up from 24, with Gen3 AI to 95% attachment. No major capacity issues; Galway/Singapore expansions meet mid-teens procedure guide. U.S. CMS tailwinds and Europe FlexiCath drive 63-65% FY24 mix, margin-accretive to 68.5%. Robotics pull-through accelerates as installs hit 4,200+.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera - Barclays:
Hi team. Tom, on hospital/ASC adoption, the ASC surge to 38% is strong—how does this impact pricing and competitive dynamics versus Mako/da Vinci?

Tom Hargrove:
Alex, spot on. ASCs average $2.8k disposables ASP +15% hospitals, bundled value prop. PrecisionNav TCO 30% lower, gaining ortho/neuro from Mako/Intuitive via Connect EHR integration +18% throughput. 42 new Q4 installs target 55% blended, $280M dispos incremental. Site-neutral OPPS amplifies.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Singh with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Priya Singh - Morgan Stanley:
Thanks. Raj, R&D at 11.2% with InnoBot and NeuroScan—timeline risks from FDA scrutiny or supply for robotics?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Priya, good one. FDA review times up 20%, but Breakthrough/IDE progress keeps NeuroScan Q4 PMA, InnoBot Q1 2025 first-in-human. NVIDIA partnership, dual rare earths mitigate supply. $1.15B FY spend yields six blockbusters, 8-10% growth engine.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver sustainable growth.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
